sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Uetze, a municipality of villages east of Hannover, has no parking rules that we could find: no tariffs, parking-disc zones, resident parking or parking-space statute, though the absence of a document does not prove there are none. Its policy is visible in the Region Hannover's transport plan and in a traffic trial. The Region's local transport plan, whose cover is dated April 2022, aims to provide park-and-ride at all rail stations close to where people live, rates Dollbergen as priority 1 for park-and-ride and bike-and-ride and Dedenhausen as priority 2 and 3, and says use of park-and-ride sites is currently free of charge, which may change, since fees could make sense for casual users of bike garages and multi-storey car parks [3][4]. From June 2024 Uetze trialled speed 20 on Kaiserstraße and one-way traffic on Bentestraße around Hindenburgplatz. The evaluation of January 2025 found no clear fall in traffic volumes but lower speeds and about 70 percent support for speed 20, and in the on-site survey 93 percent of those arriving by car found a space directly [14]. A household survey by the University of Hannover found that 56.9 percent use a car or motorbike daily or almost daily, and the authors conclude that car traffic is very important locally because public transport is weak or seen as weak [15]. The retail concept of 2019 names the centre around Hindenburgplatz as the main centre and suggests linking the Edeka customer car park with it to improve walking access, without setting any parking tariffs or zones [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is at the two stations. In October 2019 the Region's transport committee approved about 1.1 million euros in pre-financing for a Dollbergen station redesign, noting that up to 150 rail customers' cars were counted daily around the full car parks and that 133 more spaces were planned [6]. A new Dollbergen P+R area with 133 additional car spaces opened for use on 28 September 2021, on top of 84 spaces already there, with a bike facility for 160 bicycles and ten motorcycle spaces to follow [7]. The municipality announced that ground sensors for a digital parking guidance system would be installed at the northern part of the Dedenhausen lot on 9 and 10 March 2023 [9], and in June 2024 it reported more than 100 new bicycle spaces at Dedenhausen station [10]. On 21 October 2026 it reported that the electronic lock of the Dollbergen bike cage has repeatedly failed, so the Region keeps the cage open until it is fixed [11]. The first fast charging station, 2 x 50 kW, was handed over at the town hall in July 2023 [12]. A renovation of the Hannover to Berlin rail corridor from October 2026 to December 2027 will largely close the Lehrter Stammbahn to trains, with replacement buses planned, though the release does not name Dollbergen or Dedenhausen [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The counts for the two sites do not agree. The Region's portal lists P+R Dollbergen with 133 car spaces plus 2 for reduced mobility, free, with 160 roofed bike places and live free-space counts, served by RE 30 to Hannover and buses [1]. It lists P+R Dedenhausen with a headline of 62 spaces, free, in two areas that sum to 64, and its underlying data record lists 114 [2]. Deutsche Bahn lists 50 spaces at Dedenhausen and three lots with 40, 44 and 28 spaces at Dollbergen [0]. The 133 additional spaces of 2021 on top of 84 existing ones do not match the portal's 133 either, and no source explains the differences.

Our data cover both park-and-rides for about 27 days since late September 2026, using the Region's feed capacities, so the percentages are approximate. Dedenhausen (62 spaces) averaged about 20% on weekdays and 11% at weekends, with a peak of 56% on a Tuesday morning, and Dollbergen (133 spaces) 7% on weekdays and 1% at weekends, with a peak of 31%, so Dollbergen is almost empty.
